belief: I must keep the rules to stay in God’s favor.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you must keep the rules to stay in God’s favor, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A legalistic church background with long lists of do’s and don’ts. A home where approval depended on obedience. Fear of God’s anger when you slip. Measuring spirituality by outward behavior. Never fully understanding grace.
teaches: God’s commands are good, and obedience matters. But we do not earn or keep God’s favor by rule-keeping. Through faith in Christ we have peace with God and stand in grace. If righteousness came through the law, Christ died for nothing. Grace that depends on works would no longer be grace. We obey because we stand in God’s favor, not to stay there.
self_statements: One slip and I lose God’s favor.
God only likes me when I follow the rules.
I have to keep earning God’s approval.
My standing with God depends on my behavior.
If I break a rule, God turns away.
I need more rules to stay safe.
errors: Believing God’s favor depends on your record.
Believing you are either in favor or out with each action.
Obeying out of fear of losing God rather than love.
Treating Christ’s work as not enough.
questions: How do I have peace with God, according to Romans 5:1?
What would Christ’s death mean if righteousness came by rules?
Can grace depend on works and still be grace?
Am I obeying out of love or fear?
What rules have I added that God never gave?
What would obedience look like if I knew I was secure?
truth: I do not have to keep the rules to stay in God’s favor. Through faith in Christ, I have peace with God and stand in His grace. My standing depends on Jesus, not my performance. I obey God because I am loved and secure, not to earn or keep His favor.
hw_questions: How do I have peace with God?
What would Christ’s death mean if rules saved?
Am I obeying from love or fear?
What rules have I added that God didn’t give?
hw_truths: I stand in God’s grace through Christ.
I have peace with God through faith.
My standing depends on Jesus, not my record.
I obey because I am loved, not to stay loved.
Sin is not my master; I am under grace.
Grace is a gift, not a wage.
log: Each day, write one way I obeyed God out of love and one reminder that I stand in grace.
name_example: Therefore, since Sarah has been justified through faith, she has peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom she has gained access by faith into this grace in which she stands.
actions: Write down the rules you feel you must keep,
and mark which ones come from Scripture and which from people.
and write what Paul says about rules and the Spirit.
“I still stand in grace,” then take one good next step.
Do one act of obedience this week
simply out of love for God.
tracker: One act of obedience from love
prayer: Father, thank You that I stand in Your grace through Jesus. Help me reject the lie that I must keep the rules to stay in Your favor. Free me from fear-based obedience, and let my obedience flow from love and gratitude. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
